newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TINY CHESTERFIELD TAKE ON MULTINATIONAL BORO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TINY CHESTERFIELD TAKE ON MULTINATIONAL BORO.

text.p: Tiny Chesterfield will take on Middlesbrough's multinational task force in the English F.A. Cup semifinals while Chelsea will play Wimbledon in an intriguing London derby.

The draw made on Sunday pitted second division Chesterfield, in the last four for the first time in their 131-year history, against a Middlesbrough side driven by Brazilians Juninho and Emerson and 7.0 million pound ($11.2 million) striker Fabrizio Ravanelli.
Chesterfield beat Wrexham 1-0 in a quarter-final tie on Sunday while Middlesbrough won 2-0 at Derby on Saturday.
The first time Chesterfield qualified for the first round proper of the world's oldest cup competition, 102 years ago, they were drawn against Middlesbrough and lost 4-0.

But more recent history bodes well for the Derbyshire side. The last time they met Middlesbrough in the F.A. Cup, in the 1949-50 season, they won 3-2 in the fourth round to set up a clash with Chelsea.
Chelsea are due to play Wimbledon in the other semifinal after their respective victories over Portsmouth and Sheffield Wednesday on Sunday.
The two London sides met in last season's quarter-finals, Chelsea winning 3-1 in a replay after the first match ended in a 2-2 draw.
But Wimbledon won 4-2 at Stamford Bridge in the league this season and have now lost just four of their last 37 games.
"If we play as well as we did when we beat them over at Chelsea we've got half a chance," Wimbledon manager Joe Kinnear said.
Ties are due to be played on April 13 at neutral venues.
